title: Licence, Insurance, MOT & Vehicle Tax
whatItIs: To drive a car on the road you need a valid licence, insurance, vehicle tax and, once the car is 3 years old, an MOT. Police can ask to see the documents.

keyFacts.text: You MUST hold a valid licence for the vehicle category and tell DVLA if you change your name or address.
You MUST have insurance covering at least injury or damage to third parties.
Cars MUST normally pass an MOT 3 years from first registration, then every year.
Vehicle tax MUST be paid on vehicles used or kept on public roads. Untaxed and off the road: you MUST declare SORN.
You MUST produce your licence, insurance and MOT certificate if a police officer asks.

rows: Driving not in line with your licence
notes: GOV.UK: for no insurance the police can also give a £300 fixed penalty and 6 points, and can seize the vehicle.

a.label: Third-party insurance
points: Covers injury or damage to other people and property
Does not cover your own car or injury to you

b.label: Comprehensive insurance
points: Also your own car (up to its market value) and injury to you

onTheTest.question: A pupil's 4-year-old car has no current MOT certificate. When can it legally be driven on the road?
options: Within 7 days of the old MOT running out
On lessons, if a qualified supervisor is present
To a pre-arranged MOT test, or to repairs needed for it
At any time, as long as it is taxed and insured
onTheTest.why: You must not drive a car without an MOT certificate when it should have one. Exceptionally, you may drive to a pre-arranged test or to a garage for repairs needed for the test.

onTheTest.question: A police officer asks your pupil for their documents, which they do not have with them. What can happen?
options: They may be asked to take them to a police station within 7 days
They must show them within 24 hours
onTheTest.why: Highway Code annex 3: if you cannot produce your licence, insurance and MOT certificate when asked, you may be asked to take them to a police station within seven days.

traps: An unused car kept off the road MUST have either a SORN or valid insurance.
You can get an MOT up to a month (minus a day) early and keep the same renewal date.
Driving an unroadworthy car may invalidate your insurance.
Uninsured drivers can be detected by roadside cameras; the car can be seized and crushed.
